Snorkeling in Lanikai
East Oahu - Kailua Bay
Why Lanikai Beach Is a Must-Snorkel Destination on Oahu
Lanikai Beach is widely known as one of the most beautiful beaches in Hawaii — and for good reason. With its powder-soft white sand, crystal-clear turquoise waters, and the postcard-perfect view of the
Mokulua Islands
, it’s a favorite for locals and visitors alike. But beyond its beauty,
Lanikai offers exceptional snorkeling opportunities
, especially when conditions are calm.
You can expect:
Excellent visibility on light wind days
Shallow coral reef formations
Frequent sightings of tropical fish and Hawaiian green sea turtles (honu)
But here’s the catch:
Lanikai is located in a residential neighborhood with extremely limited parking.
So how do you explore this slice of paradise without the stress?
Rent your snorkel gear and a beach cruiser from us and bike over like a local.
🐠 What You’ll See Snorkeling at Lanikai
Lanikai’s underwater environment is gentle and accessible, making it ideal for beginner and intermediate snorkelers. Depending on ocean conditions, you may encounter:
Yellow tang, parrotfish, and triggerfish
Honu (Hawaiian sea turtles)
Small reef formations and coral heads
Calm currents with excellent visibility
Best conditions:
Mornings (before trade winds pick up)
Days with low surf and gentle, incoming tides
When the water is clear and the sky is sunny
🌿 Respect the Reef, the Community, and the Aloha Spirit
Lanikai is not just a beach — it’s a residential neighborhood. As a visitor, it’s important to practice
responsible tourism
and
marine conservation
:
Use
reef-safe sunscreen
(available at Kailua Beach Adventures)
Never stand on or touch coral
Use public beach access paths only
Pack out all trash and leave no trace
Keep voices down and respect local residents
🧭 Planning Your Day: What to Bring
To make the most of your snorkeling adventure:
Refillable water bottle
Towel or pareo
Hat and sunglasses
Dry bag for keys/phone
Waterproof camera or GoPro (optional)
Light snack or post-snorkel treat
Tip: Kailua Beach Adventures also rents
kayaks
,
SUPs
, and
beach chairs
, so you can plan a full beach day.
📍 Why Choose Kailua Beach Adventures?
Kailua Beach Adventures has been serving locals and visitors for over 30 years. Their expert staff offers:
Up-to-date ocean safety tips
Local knowledge on best snorkel spots
Friendly customer service and flexible rentals
Free parking, changing rooms, and gear orientation
Whether you're new to snorkeling or a seasoned swimmer, they’ll help you plan your
perfect Lanikai snorkel day.

Kailua Beach Park is one of the largest and nicest beach parks on Oahu’s Windward Side. Located towards the southern end of Kailua Bay, Kailua Beach Park offers plenty of shade, white sand beaches, and a perfect swimming area for keiki (kids). The most popular activities include kayaking, stand up paddling, and kitesurfing, as well as large, natural sand beaches for sun tanning and relaxing. The largest annual event at Kailua Beach Park is the fireworks display on the fourth of July. The whole town plus visitors come out to watch a spectacular display of fireworks over the bay.
Location
Kailua is 12 miles from Waikiki and about a 30-minute drive over the Pali Highway. Kailua Beach stretches for approximately 2.5 miles and lies just north of Lanikai Beach, ranked number 1 and 2 attractions in Kailua on TripAdvisor. Currently, no commercial drop-offs are allowed at the beach park, so using the City Bus or taking a car are currently the only ways to get here:
By Car
:
From Waikiki: Head east on H1 freeway, take exit 21A for Pali Highway towards Kailua, follow the signs for Kailua, continue on Pali Highway for about 6 miles, then turn left onto Kailua Road, and continue straight for about 2 miles until you reach the beach park.
From Honolulu: Take H1 eastbound, take exit 21A for Pali Highway towards Kailua, follow the signs for Kailua, continue on Pali Highway for about 6 miles, then turn left onto Kailua Road, and continue straight for about 2 miles until you reach the beach park.
By Public Transit:
From Waikiki: Take TheBus route 22 or 57 to Kailua Transit Center, then transfer to route 70 or 77 and get off at Kailua Beach Park stop.
From Honolulu: Take TheBus route 57 to Kailua Transit Center, then transfer to route 70 or 77 and get off at Kailua Beach Park stop.
If you're staying in Kailua or Lanikai, the beach park is easily accessible by bike or foot.

Description
Want to feel like you're walking on water? Experience Kailua's stunning waters on a Stand Up Paddleboard (SUP). Our range of SUP rentals includes a variety of light and easy-to-use boards, ranging from 10’2”,10’6”ft to 11ft all-around paddle boards. Whether you're a beginner or a seasoned pro, Kailua's diverse SUP conditions cater to all experience levels.
Join the fastest-growing water sport in Kailua and discover the joys of SUP!

What's Included

Destinations
Beginner stand-up paddleboarders start in the canal to practice technique and balance before heading out to the ocean. Kailua offers over a mile of inland canals that can be utilized for flat water exploration. Traveling to the mouth of the canal, you will end up at Kailua Beach, which is the best launch site to visit Flat Island. This is a short paddle and worth the effort. Landing at a small cove on the island allows a chance for a break and to explore the seabird sanctuary island by foot. Next, paddle along Lanikai’s turquoise, calm water, offering views of the coral reef, tropical fish, and meandering sea turtles. For the experienced stand-up paddler, SUP out to the ‘Twin Islands’ or Mokulua’s for a real adventure!
Policy, Restrictions
There is a $10 cancellation fee per piece of equipment if the rental is cancelled on the day of.
There is no charge for day-before (before 12:00 am) cancellation. All participants must be able to swim.
Paddleboarding is a physical activity that does require a moderate level of fitness. SUPs must also be transported via cart to the beach (5-10 min walk).
